newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand temporarily reduces copper cathode tariff.
newsitem.headline: Thailand temporarily reduces copper cathode tariff.

text.p: Thailand will temporarily cut the import tariff on copper cathode to 1.0 percent from the current 6.0 percent, a government official said on Tuesday.
The cut, which was approved by the cabinet on Tuesday, will be in effect through December 31, 1998.
The move is to help reduce production costs of electric appliances and electronic products, a government official said.
Thailand's first copper smelter, developed by unlisted Thai Copper Industries, will come on stream by October, 1998.

Planned full capacity of 165,000 tonnes of cathodes a year should be reached a year after the $600 million smelter starts operating, Thai Copper Industries chairman and chief executive Prayudh Mahagitsiri told Reuters earlier on Tuesday.
All copper produced at the smelter will be sold in Thailand.
Local demand for copper cathode soared to a projected 195,000 tonnes in 1996 from 30,000 tonnes in 1989, industry sources said.
